messages:
shivam: Quick Q — I'm about to land a Terraform change that moves some ExternalSecret wiring out of annotations into .spec.template so we can set per-key TTL + KMS context. Before I flip it across clusters, curious about rotation behavior and any migration pitfalls. cc @elaine @corey

elaine: I did a small spike yesterday. operator supports `.spec.template` (it's cleaner). A couple of gotchas: 1) Vault lease TTL is independent — operator just fetches the secret and writes it into k8s. 2) The ExternalSecret `refreshInterval` controls how often the operator re-reads Vault, so set that to match your expected rotation cadence.

corey: Also note: annotations were our historical migration hack. If you switch to templates the operator will start managing the secret values there but won't automatically delete annotation-backed keys. migration step needed or we'll have duplicate keys.

shivam: good to know. what about rendered templates? any syntax differences?

elaine: use `{{ .Data.foo }}` inside the template. If you need KMSEncryptionContext, add it as part of the template metadata or use the provider config. Example tested:

```
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: svc-db-creds
spec:
  refreshInterval: "30m"
  secretStoreRef:
    name: vault-store
    kind: SecretStore
  target:
    name: svc-db-creds
    creationPolicy: Owner
    template:
      type: Opaque
      data:
        username: "{{ .Data.username }}"
        password: "{{ .Data.password }}"
      # per-key annotations allowed here if you need special handling
  data:
    - secretKey: username
      remoteRef:
        key: secret/data/services/svc-db
        property: username
    - secretKey: password
      remoteRef:
        key: secret/data/services/svc-db
        property: password
```

elaine: That template block is what we want instead of stuffing JSON into annotations.

corey: FYI — operator versions <1.7 had a bug where TTL-based reconciliation could be off by a minute. Make sure the cluster is on >=1.8. I can confirm our staging cluster is on 1.9.

infra-bot: cluster-check: external-secrets-operator version=1.9.2, pods=external-secrets-operator-0 (Running), lastRestart=2026-02-12T10:04:22Z. No recent errors matching "vault.*lease" in logs.

kevin: Will the TF diff be a disruptive rollout? I pushed a branch that adds `spec.template` while leaving annotations in place for now. Plan was: 1) add template + short refreshInterval in TF, 2) run a migration job, 3) remove annotations after one week. Thoughts?

corey: That's the safe path. For the migration job I recommend a k8s Job that: reads existing secret (if present), writes the same content to the new ExternalSecret managed Secret target, and annotates it with `migration.redwood.com/from-annotations=true`. Keep the job idempotent.

shivam: i'll sketch that job. also question re: RBAC — does operator need any extra perms for creating Secrets when switching to template? I thought it already needed create/update secrets perms.

elaine: correct — it needs secrets/create, update, patch. No change. But if you change ownerReferences behaviour (creationPolicy) to Owner, operator will set owner refs on the managed Secret — make sure Controller has `ownerreferences` rights (it's fine for standard manifests).

kevin: I'll open the TF PR now: #789 (wip). Ping me if you want me to split the change into two PRs (infra + migration job).

shivam: Example small migration helper (pseudo):

```
#!/bin/bash
set -e
NAMESPACE=platform
for s in $(kubectl -n $NAMESPACE get secret -l app=svc-db -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
  echo "migrating $s"
  kubectl -n $NAMESPACE get secret $s -o yaml | \ 
    yq e '.metadata.annotations["migration.redwood.com/from-annotations"] = "true"' - | \
    kubectl apply -f -
done
```

shivam: (this job will be wrapped in a k8s Job with SA that has minimal perms)

elaine: smoke test: after migration, curl the app endpoint that depends on the secret and ensure 200. Also check `kubectl get secret <name> -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 --decode` to verify content.

corey: One more note — if a secret is large or you have many keys, template rendering could hit size limits on k8s Secrets. Not likely here, but worth checking.

kevin: tagging @platform-owners to keep them in the loop. I'll add a short checklist to the PR.

shivam: action items: 1) kevin opens TF PR with templates added but annotations retained (PR #789) 2) elaine will author migration Job manifest as a followup 3) corey will validate operator version on prod clusters and check logs 4) shivam will run the migration in staging and run smoke tests.

elaine: i'll do the migration job this afternoon, review expected logs, and add runbook steps for rollback. :thumbsup:

kevin: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/789 — marked wip, added checklist.

shivam: thanks all. i'll wait for your reviews before rolling to prod.

shivam: noted. end of thread.
